claim: Annual general sessions begin on the day in January set by statute
quote: Annual general sessions of the Legislature shall be held at the seat of government and shall begin on the day in January designated by statute.

claim: The annual general session begins the first Tuesday after the third Monday in January
quote: The annual general session of the Legislature shall begin the first Tuesday after the third Monday in January.

claim: A general session may not exceed 45 calendar days, excluding holidays
quote: no annual general session of the Legislature may exceed 45 calendar days, excluding state holidays and federal holidays

claim: The legislature can convene itself on a two-thirds poll for a fiscal crisis or emergency
quote: two-thirds of all members elected to each house are in favor of convening the Legislature into session

claim: A bill not returned within ten days (Sundays and day received excepted) becomes law
quote: If any bill is not returned by the governor within ten days after it has been presented to the governor, Sunday and the day it was received excepted, it shall become a law without a signature.

claim: After adjournment the governor has twenty days to file objections
quote: it shall become a law unless the governor within twenty days after adjournment files the objections to it

claim: Acts take effect sixty days after adjournment unless two-thirds of each house direct otherwise
quote: no act shall take effect until sixty days after the adjournment of the session at which it passed

claim: The regular general election is in November of even-numbered years
quote: A regular general election shall be held throughout the state on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year.

claim: County officers and local school board members are chosen at the regular general election
quote: county officers; State School Board members; local school board members

claim: Municipal general elections are in November of odd-numbered years, with odd-year special district elections
quote: a municipal general election shall be held in municipalities, and special districts as applicable, on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered year

claim: The regular primary is the fourth Tuesday of June in even years, for national, state, school board and county offices
quote: The regular primary election shall be held throughout the state on the fourth Tuesday of June of each even numbered year

claim: A municipal primary, if necessary, is the second Tuesday after the first Monday in August
quote: A municipal primary election shall be held, if necessary, on the second Tuesday following the first Monday in August before the regular municipal election

claim: Municipal officers serve four-year terms beginning the first Monday in January
quote: The officers elected shall continue in the office to which they were elected for four years

claim: In five- and six-member council cities, about half the council and the mayor are elected the year after a presidential election
quote: in the year following a year in which a presidential election is held, the offices of: approximately half the council members

claim: Special district board elections are held with the municipal general election or the regular general election
quote: at the same time as the municipal general election or the regular general election, as applicable

claim: Special district candidates go in the nonpartisan section of the ballot
quote: in the nonpartisan section of the ballot

claim: Special district board terms are four years
quote: the term of each member of a board of trustees is four years

claim: Party candidates for county and other regular offices are nominated in a regular primary
quote: Candidates for elective office that are to be filled at the next regular general election shall be nominated in a regular primary election by direct vote of the people

claim: Each party declares which other parties' members, and whether unaffiliated voters, may vote for its candidates
quote: identify one or more registered political parties whose members may vote for the registered political party's candidates and whether individuals identified as unaffiliated with a political party may vote for the registered political party's candidates

claim: A candidate may not appear as the candidate of more than one party
quote: appear on the ballot as the candidate of more than one political party

claim: A signer of a party nomination petition may not sign another candidate's petition for the same office
quote: may not sign a petition to nominate another candidate for the same office

claim: Local school board candidates are nonpartisan and nominated in the regular primary
quote: candidates for nonpartisan local school board positions to advance to the regular general election

claim: All municipal candidates are nominated at a municipal primary
quote: Candidates for municipal office in all municipalities shall be nominated at a municipal primary election.

claim: There is no municipal primary if candidates do not exceed twice the seats
quote: If the number of candidates for a particular municipal office does not exceed twice the number of individuals needed to fill that office, a primary election for that office may not be held and the candidates are considered nominated.

claim: Third, fourth and fifth class cities and towns may instead nominate by municipal party convention or committee
quote: any third, fourth, or fifth class city or town may exempt itself from a primary election by providing that the nomination of candidates for municipal office to be voted upon at a municipal election be nominated by a municipal party convention or committee

claim: When a municipality nominates by convention, the party name appears with the candidate's name
quote: When a municipality has chosen to nominate candidates by convention or committee, the election officer shall ensure that the party name is included with the candidate's name on the ballot

claim: City officers are elected at large unless the city provides for districts by ordinance
quote: the officers of each city shall be elected in an at-large election held at the time and in the manner provided for electing municipal officers

claim: A city may elect some or all council members by district by ordinance
quote: The governing body of a city may by ordinance provide for the election of some or all commissioners or council members, as the case may be, by district

claim: Municipal candidates must have lived in the municipality for 12 months
quote: has resided within the municipality in which the individual seeks to hold elective office for the 12 consecutive months immediately before the date of the election

claim: The candidate with the most votes is elected or nominated
quote: the person receiving the highest number of votes at any: election for any office to be filled at that election is elected to that office

claim: The municipal alternate voting methods (ranked-choice) pilot has been repealed
quote: before the pilot project was repealed, the Municipal Alternate Voting Methods Pilot Project

claim: Candidates who do not affiliate with a party may get on the ballot by certificate of nomination
quote: Candidates for public office who do not wish to affiliate with a registered political party may obtain a position on the ballot by following the procedures and requirements of this part.

claim: A candidate who filed a declaration of candidacy may not file as unaffiliated the same year
quote: A candidate who has filed a declaration of candidacy may not file a certificate of nomination as an unaffiliated candidate in the same year.

claim: Signing an unaffiliated petition more than once for the same candidate is a misdemeanor
quote: more than once for the same candidate

claim: Counties are recognized subdivisions and continue until changed by statute
quote: The counties now existing shall continue until changed as provided by statute.

claim: The legislature provides optional forms of county government subject to voter approval
quote: The selection of an optional form shall be subject to voter approval as provided by statute.

claim: Counties choose among four forms: commission, expanded commission, executive-council, council-manager
quote: the county commission form under Section 17-62-201 ; the expanded county commission form under Section 17-62-202 ; the county executive and council form under Section 17-62-203 ; or the council-manager form under Section 17-62-204

claim: A county uses the three-member commission form unless it adopts another
quote: Unless a county adopts another form of government as provided in this chapter, the county shall operate under the county commission form of government

claim: The commission form has three commissioners serving as both legislative body and executive
quote: A county commission consisting of three members shall govern each county operating under the county commission form of government.

claim: Commissioners serve four-year staggered terms and are elected at large unless a court orders otherwise
quote: the term of office of each county commission member is four years

claim: The expanded commission form has five or seven commissioners
quote: A county commission consisting of five or seven members shall govern each county operating under an expanded county commission form of government.

claim: An optional plan may not provide for nonpartisan election of county officers
quote: provides for the nonpartisan election of elected officers

claim: A county with partisan elections may not change to nonpartisan elections
quote: A county that provides for the election of the county's elected officers through a partisan election may not change to a process that provides for the election of the county's elected officers through a nonpartisan election.

claim: Fifth and sixth class counties may only use the commission or expanded commission form
quote: for a county of the fifth or sixth class: the county commission form under Section 17-62-201 ; or the expanded county commission form under Section 17-62-202

claim: Elected county officers include the assessor, attorney, auditor, clerk, recorder, sheriff, surveyor and treasurer
quote: the county assessor, with powers and duties described in Chapter 67, County Assessor

claim: Counties under the executive-council or council-manager form elect council members and a county executive
quote: the county legislative body members and the county executive

claim: Elected county officers are elected every four years at the regular general election
quote: each elected county officer shall be elected at the regular general election every four years

claim: A county may consolidate county offices by ordinance
quote: consolidates county offices and establishes the duties of consolidated county offices

claim: Counties are classified by population into six classes
quote: A county with a population less than 5,000 is a county of the sixth class.

claim: Municipalities are classified by population: first class city at 100,000
quote: A municipality with a population of 100,000 or more is a city of the first class.

claim: Fifth class city is 1,000 to 9,999
quote: A municipality with a population of 1,000 or more but less than 10,000 is a city of the fifth class.

claim: A municipality under 1,000 is a town
quote: A municipality with a population under 1,000 is a town.

claim: A municipality keeps its class until changed through the lieutenant governor's certificate
quote: Each municipality shall retain its classification under Section 10-2-301 until changed as provided in this section

claim: Any city or town may adopt a charter through an elected charter commission
quote: Any incorporated city or town may frame and adopt a charter for its own government

claim: Charter commission candidates run without party designation
quote: but without party designation

claim: Municipal forms include council-mayor, six-member council and five-member council
quote: "Council-mayor form of government" means the form of municipal government that

claim: A council-mayor form may not be adopted without voter approval
quote: may not be adopted without voter approval

claim: School boards have five, seven or nine members depending on enrollment
quote: The board of education of a school district with a student population of less than 10,000 students comprises five members.

claim: School board members are elected at each regular general election, staggered
quote: Members of a local board of education shall be elected at each regular general election.

claim: School board members serve four-year terms
quote: The term of office for an individual elected to a local board of education is four years

claim: School boards are elected from board districts drawn by the county or city
quote: shall divide the local school district into local school board districts

claim: Title 17 county sections were renumbered in the 2025 special session
quote: Renumbered and Amended by Chapter

claim: The council-mayor form has two separate, independent and equal branches
quote: consists of two separate, independent, and equal branches of municipal government
